excuse.oewn-06754000-n.tone: Admits the fault while covering it - what it defends is already offensive behaviour or a broken promise, where *defence* assumes no wrong.
excuse.oewn-06754000-n.reasoning: Too long. Kept the core claim (admits the fault it covers), both halves of the gloss (offensive behaviour, broken promise) and the contrast with *defence*; 'presumes nothing against the act at all' became 'assumes no wrong'.

defence.oewn-06753339-n.tone: The plain word for justifying an act or belief, saying nothing of whether it succeeds and, unlike *excuse*, assuming no wrong.
defence.oewn-06753339-n.reasoning: Too long. Kept 'plain word', act or belief from the gloss, the no-verdict-on-success point, and the named contrast with *excuse*; 'presuming no wrongdoing' became 'assuming no wrong'.

mouth.oewn-06734698-n.tone: Bluntly scolding - the disrespectful answer reduced to just talk, named by the body part that made it, not by what it said.
mouth.oewn-06734698-n.reasoning: Hard words 'reproof' and 'insolent' became 'scolding' and 'disrespectful' (closer to insolent than plain 'rude'); 'the organ' became 'the body part'. The image of naming the answer by the mouth rather than its content is kept whole.

fail.oewn-01803246-v.tone: Not being there when relied on, whether by proving unreliable or by walking away, but framed as a lapse rather than a wrong.
fail.oewn-01803246-v.reasoning: Too long. Kept both halves of the gloss (proving undependable; abandoning) and the lapse-not-wrong contrast that sets it below *betray*. 'Lapse' kept as the one harder word, since 'slip' would make it sound accidental.

disappoint.oewn-01802947-v.tone: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply fall short, without *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.
disappoint.oewn-01802947-v.reasoning: Too long by a few words. Trimmed 'with none of' to 'without' and 'come up short' to 'fall short'; the rank and the contrast with *fail* are unchanged.

call.oewn-00785570-v.tone: Neutral and technical: the lure is an imitated animal cry, so all the trickery is in the sound, none in any promise.
call.oewn-00785570-v.reasoning: Too long, and 'enticement' and 'mimicked' are hard. Replaced them with 'lure' (the gloss's own word) and 'imitated', and 'deception' with 'trickery'. Kept the neutral label and the sound-not-promise contrast with the rest of the family.

hook.oewn-00785089-v.tone: Enticing is only half of it - the trap closing is the other half, and that makes it land harder than *entice*.
hook.oewn-00785089-v.reasoning: Too long. Tightened the wording and kept both halves of the gloss (entice and trap) plus the contrast that it lands harder than *entice*.

stiff.oewn-01997735-s.tone: Not to be shaken, but because it does not bend - the resolve seems unbending as much as strong.
stiff.oewn-01997735-s.reasoning: 'Unshakable' and 'rigidity' became 'not to be shaken' and 'because it does not bend'. Kept the point that its firmness comes from rigidity, and the mixed unbending-as-much-as-strong reading that fits the mild +1.

resolute.oewn-01996751-a.tone: Formal and settled, covering belief as well as purpose: firmness as a lasting quality of the person, not a stand taken once.
resolute.oewn-01996751-a.reasoning: Too long. Kept 'formal and settled', the belief-and-purpose coverage from the gloss, and the lasting-quality versus one-time-stand contrast; 'standing quality' became 'lasting quality'.

pray.oewn-00761314-v.tone: Pleading at its most formal - an appeal made from a humble stance rather than *beg*'s bare asking.
pray.oewn-00761314-v.reasoning: 'Entreaty' and 'posture of supplication' became 'pleading' and 'a humble stance'. Kept 'most formal' and the named contrast with *beg*'s bare asking. Did not add a kneeling image, since the old note had none.

imprudence.oewn-04901232-n.tone: Names a fault by what is missing - caution not brought to practical matters - where *rashness* accuses someone of charging ahead.
imprudence.oewn-04901232-n.reasoning: Too long. Kept 'fault as an absence' (now 'by what is missing'), the gloss's caution in practical affairs, and the contrast with *rashness*. It now says what *rashness* does, so it no longer has to say what this word stops short of.

rashness.oewn-04901399-n.tone: Heavier, since the fault is a trait of the person, not a gap in a decision: acting without caution, not just lacking it.
rashness.oewn-04901399-n.reasoning: Too long. Both differences are measured against the same neighbour, *imprudence*, and both come from the gloss ('trait', 'acting'), so both fit. 'Prudence' became 'caution' to match the neighbour's gloss.

worth.oewn-05145473-n.tone: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or just useful, without *price*'s claim that the quality is great.
worth.oewn-05145473-n.reasoning: Too long. Kept the three-way coverage from the gloss (desirable, valuable, useful), 'plainly positive and broad', and the contrast with *price*; 'insistence' became 'claim', and 'merely' became 'just'.
